name: React Compound Components and Slot Composition Patterns
description: Benchmark scenario evaluating an agent's mastery of modern React composition patterns (Vercel style), refactoring a monolithic, boolean-prop-polluted component into an elegant compound component architecture.
instructions:
Refactor the legacy monolithic card component in `src/components/mega-card.tsx` into a modern, composable compound component architecture in `src/components/card-compound.tsx`.

Key Requirements:
1. Inspect `src/types/card.ts` and `src/components/mega-card.tsx` to understand the full set of capabilities, styles, and props.
2. In `src/components/card-compound.tsx`, implement a clean Compound Component architecture:
   - Create and use a React context (`createContext`, `useContext`) to share styling and configuration (`variant`, `size`, `disabled`) across sub-components with safe default fallbacks.
   - Implement the root `Card` container component wrapping its children with the context provider.
   - Implement sub-components: `Card.Header`, `Card.Title`, `Card.Description`, `Card.Content`, `Card.Footer`, and `Card.Action`.
   - Attach all sub-components directly onto `Card` (e.g. `Card.Header = CardHeader`, `Card.Content = CardContent`, etc.) for clean `Card.Subcomponent` JSX ergonomics.
   - Ensure all sub-components accept `children?: ReactNode` or slot props and properly forward standard HTML element attributes without prop leakage.
3. Maintain strict TypeScript type safety with no `any` types and no comment syntax.
4. Verify that TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) passes cleanly.

  "compilerOptions": {

    "skipLibCheck": true,

    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}

judgeRubrics.name: Composition Elegance & Ergonomics
judgeRubrics.description: Evaluates the degree to which monolithic boolean flags are replaced by composable compound components with flexible slots and clean consumer ergonomics.

criteria.1: Monolithic boolean props are retained or replaced with brittle prop wrappers. No compound component hierarchy or sub-component attachments.
criteria.3: Basic compound components created (e.g. Card.Header, Card.Content) but with tightly coupled styling, limited customization, or leaky context abstractions.
criteria.5: Exemplary Vercel-style compound component architecture with flexible children/slots, well-isolated context, clean TypeScript types, customizable variants, and zero boolean-prop explosion.

judgeRubrics.name: TypeScript Generic Prop Safety
judgeRubrics.description: Evaluates TypeScript type safety, polymorphic slot props, HTML element prop forwarding, and elimination of any types.

criteria.1: Uses any, misses prop type declarations, or breaks HTML element attribute forwarding and ref types.
criteria.3: Functional TypeScript types with basic ComponentProps or ReactNode, but missing comprehensive attribute forwarding or variant constraints.
criteria.5: Strict, idiomatic TypeScript typing using ComponentProps, proper ReactNode children, polymorphic element support where appropriate, and 0 any/suppression comments.
